races.name: Churchill Tyres Apprentice Handicap
races.verdict: SNOOKER MCCREW had a bit to spare when an all-the-way winner at Kempton last week and might be able to defy the penalty. Tiberio Force is respected on the back of his Ripon classified win, while an unexposed profile provides hope that Star Suepreme may build on last week's course success.

runners.note: Back to winning ways in Ripon classified event (1¼m, soft) 22 days ago, his second successive success in that contest. After last year's win he went on to finish second in a handicap on his next start. Enters calculation
Came good at the fourth time of asking for current yard in 1m Kempton apprentice handicap under Alfie Redman last week. Had a bit to spare so a 5-lb penalty shouldn't prevent another bold bid.
Remains winless. Creditable fourth over this trip at Ayr last month but not so good at Carlisle and Redcar since.
Much improved with cheekpieces added (retained) when winning a course handicap (8.5f, good) last Wednesday. A 6-lb penalty demands further progress but she is much less exposed than most of these.
Little form of worth, including well held in 2 handicaps 10 months apart.
NON RUNNER.

Sole success came over C&D last summer. Not at that level this season, including well held behind Tiberio Force at Ripon last time. It remains to be seen whether a return to Beverley sparks a revival.
Placed twice in handicaps over this trip at the start of the summer. A couple of lesser efforts have followed over 1½m at Chepstow since, although soft ground may not have suited latterly.
Maiden after 11 starts but not long with this yard. Finished 4¾ lengths behind Star Suepreme when seventh  over 8.5f here last week but the return to a longer trip should suit.
Signed off for Alan Brown with a very good second over C&D last June but hasn't offered much in 3 outings for new yard this year.
Has shown more temperament than ability.
Successful in nurseries at Chelmsford and Newcastle in 2025 but has shown nothing this season, including for this yard last 4 starts.
Well held at long odds on all 4 starts, including a Ripon classified stakes latest. Significant improvement will be needed.

races.name: SIS Irish EBF Maiden
races.verdict: SPEAKERS CORNER clearly didn't give his running despite having the worst of the draw at Glorious Goodwood 52 days ago and with his debut effort at the Curragh previously a promising one, he's fancied to bounce back with first-time blinkers now enlisted. Loughrea N Roll following his very good debut third looks a big threat though, with Churchill Bond also fancied to feature.

runners.note: Foaled April 4. 50,000 gns 2-y-o, Blue Point gelding. Half-brother to 3 winners, including 11.3f winner Vauntingly and winner up to 1¼m Hype, both useful. Dam, maiden (stayed 1½m), half-sister to very smart sprinter King
Cheap purchase who was sent off at huge odds and always behind following a very slow start when thirteenth of 15 in a Gowran maiden (7f) 3 weeks ago.
Starspangledbanner colt who showed only greenness when not knocked about tenth of 11 in a Curragh maiden (7f) 44 days ago. In top hands though, and he ought to be capable of better.

145,000 gns Lope De Vega colt who produced a promising first effort having been found wanting for know-how early doors when third of 11 in a Curragh maiden (7f) last month, running on. Looks sure to improve from that ini

Promising first effort when considerately-handled fourth (beaten 3 lengths) of 6 at the Curragh (7f). Had worst of the draw but possibly amiss when last of 13 at Goodwood (7f) 52 days ago and he certainly remains with po

€300,000 breeze-up acquisition who matched previous best when keeping on third of 12 in a Galway maiden (7f, soft) 2 weeks ago. Very shrewd stable now reach for a first-time visor and another fancied to be on the premise

races.name: Man Commercial Protection Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
races.verdict: Tricky stuff, but KIWI DE COTTE has the potential to be better than his mark over fences and the dual point/hurdles winner can make a successful return to chasing.

runners.note: Won both completed starts in points/shaped well in hunter chase on Rules debut and successful twice over hurdles at Market Rasen (23f) for new yard this summer, in first-time cheekpieces when beating 2 subsequent winners

Belatedly opened account in 19f Downpatrick maiden hurdle in June. Fair runs in handicaps the last twice and of a similar standard over fences. Probably on a fair mark starting out for new yard (bought from Gavin Cromwel

Brought up a quick-fire 5-timer in May/June (4 wins at Hexham). Poor runs at Cartmel the last twice but his solid jumping should stand him in good stead around Warwick and he shouldn't be written off back against the nov

races.name: Old Gravel Pits Lodges EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
races.verdict: ARTHURIAN sets a tall standard judged on his third in listed company at Haydock 17 days ago and looks the way to go returned to calmer waters. Bayraktar appeals as the lead danger following his York debut second, whilst Austin looks sure to build on his opening run at Haydock.

runners.note: Camelot colt who matched debut form when second in a Haydock maiden (1m) in August and then found a chunk of improvement upped markedly in grade when third of 5 in listed company back over that C&D (soft) 17 days ago. Se

Lope De Vega colt from a useful home-bred family who ran as if in need of run for fitness/experience but clearly has ability, catching the eye with his mid-race move before that effort took its toll. Imposing type who lo

State of Rest colt who was conspicuously green early but produced a promising first effort nevertheless when second in a class 2 York maiden (7f) 16 days ago, noted doing good late work. Increase in trip looks sure to su

Son of Space Traveller who offered little starting out in selling company when ninth of 12 in a 6f contest at Chester back in May. Takes a significant step up in trip (also gelded) on return from a break but yard look to

races.name: betting.bet Free Racing Tips Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle
races.verdict: VIRTUAL ROCK defied big odds with a bit up his sleeve at Uttoxeter last week and looks capable of defying a penalty providing he continues to stand regular racing. Tilehurst has form figures of 12 since the cheekpieces went on and seems sure to give another good account.

runners.note: Useful on the Flat and belied long odds as he built on his Cartmel showing on the back of another stable switch (formerly with John Butler) when winning 12-runner handicap hurdle at Uttoxeter (2½m, good) last week, well

Most progressive since returning from an absence, following up from Plumpton in emphatic fashion in 17f amateur riders handicap at Cartmel. Most likely found race coming too soon when well beaten there just 2 days later,

Recorded a first success since his bumper debut in 2m Worcester handicap in July, finding generously in first-time cheekpieces. Ran at least as well from a 7 lb higher mark when runner-up back there 18 days ago and can r

Doubled his hurdles tally at Ludlow (21f) last October and has run well in defeat a couple of times since, latterly when runner-up over C&D in June. In the mix if resuming from a break in similar form.

Fairly useful Flat winner who stepped up plenty on his hurdling debut form faced with a suitably sharp test (also hooded) when second in 6-runner novice at Worcester (2m) in May, albeit seemingly worried out of it. Makes

races.name: Rose Hotel Handicap (0-60)
races.verdict: Lots with chances but IMPERIAL DREAM rates the pick of the weights on the back of a resurgent Galway second so edges the vote. Sand Art gained a breakthrough success at Sligo last time and rates a big threat with that form having been well advertised since. Both She's On The Ball and Sceitimini can also play a prominent role. Cisterna completes the shortlist.

runners.note: Twenty two runs since last win in 2023. 10/3, respectable seventh of 13 in handicap at Limerick (7f, good to soft) in June. Needs to build on it.
Posted good second in 1m Bellewstown claimer in July on final run for Adrian McGuinness. Disappointing back in handicaps first 3 starts for new yard so others appeal more.
Comfortably scored at Roscommon in May. Largely in good form since and beaten ½ length by She's On The Ball in 22-runner handicap at Cork (7f, soft) 13 days ago. Needs considering.

Losing run is mounting up but not discredited on his last 3 starts, third of 10 in handicap at Laytown (7f) 12 days ago. Regular blinkers are refitted so not out of things. Engaged Listowel 1.53 Monday.
Fifteen runs since his last win in 2024 but best effort of the season with second of 11 in handicap at Galway (7f, soft) 14 days ago. Weighted to go well off the same mark.
Good fourth at Gowran (7f) in August but only twelfth of 16 in handicap at Cork (1m, good to soft) 23 days ago. Bounce back is needed.
Thirteen runs since her last win in 2025 but back on song with third of 10 in claimer at Laytown (6f) 12 days ago, running on. Needs to back it up now.
Unreliable individual. Fared better than of late when eighth of 14 in handicap at Roscommon (7f, good to soft) 22 days ago. Needs to build on it. Engaged Listowel 1.53 Monday.

Best effort of the summer in first-time cheekpieces when fifth of 16 in handicap at Cork (1m, good to soft) 10 days ago, albeit not fully convincing with his stamina for the longer trip. Not out of things back to 7f.
Tongue tied for first time when getting off the mark in 22-runner handicap at Cork (7f, soft) 13 days ago by ½ length from Cisterna. Up 6 lb but she can go well again in retained headgear.
On a long losing sequence but returned from 12 months off with a good fifth of 14 in handicap at Roscommon (7f, good to soft) 22 days ago, not enjoying a smooth passage last 1f. Can't be dismissed.
Scored at Naas in June. Below-form twelfth of 27 in handicap at the Curragh (6f, good) 31 days ago. Needs to get back on track.
Still a maiden but advanced his form with ½-length third of 22 to She's On The Ball in handicap at Cork (7f, soft) 13 days ago. One to consider despite 4 lb rise.

Blinkered for first time when getting off the mark at the eighth attempt in 12-runner handicap at Sligo (6f, good to soft) in August. That form has been franked so he's a player despite 3 lb rise with cheekpieces on now.
Lightly-raced maiden. Fifteenth of 16 in handicap at Cork (1m, good to soft) 23 days ago. Has work to do.
Winner at Gowran in April. Off 4 months, respectable ninth of 16 in handicap there (1m, good to soft) 21 days ago. Can take a step forward. RESERVE

Gained a first win at Bellewstown (1m) in July. Shaped encouragingly when tenth of 22 to She's On The Ball in handicap at Cork (7f, soft) 13 days ago, finishing well after suffering a poor run from 2f out. Very much one
In good form without winning until a below-par fourteenth of 22 in handicap at Cork (7f, soft) 13 days ago. Cheekpieces are reached for first time now. RESERVE

races.name: Molson Coors Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Chase
races.verdict: Not a strong handicap chase on paper and MALINAS GLORY could be the way to go as he looks on a good mark having been first past the post in a hunter here when last seen in the spring. Saint Arion makes a quick switch to fences for his in-form stable and may have found a good opening if leaving his previous form behind in first-time cheekpieces.

runners.note: Little impact in point/bumper but has shown a bit in maiden/novice hurdles this summer and, fitted with headgear, is quite an interesting chasing debutant in the context of this race. Market check advised.

Won a couple of 3-runner points in April and first past the post in 3m hunter here in May (subsequently disqualified) for Hannah Lewis. Looks ahead of his mark on that showing back down in trip after 4½ months off.
Won handicap chases at Southwell and Doncaster last season. No show last 3 starts, including on return from 5 months off at Cartmel (usual mistakes), although yard among the winners since.
Off the mark at second time of asking over fences at Newton Abbot (21f) last June. Several decent runs in defeat since and has dipped below that winning mark. Goes back up in trip.

Temperamental veteran who increasingly looks flattered by his Ludlow hunter third in April, brushed aside from 2 out after forcing the pace fitted with new headgear at Bangor when last seen 3 months ago.

Successful 3 times over 2½m last season, including in this race, though largely very disappointing since. Has dropped a long way in the weights (13 lb lower than for last year's victory) if staging a revival in first-tim

Long-standing maiden (including in points) but returned to form in a change of headgear from 5 lb out of the handicap when third at Worcester (2m) 3 weeks ago, not going down without a fight having dictated matters until

races.name: Christmas Parties R Us Restricted Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
races.verdict: If CALL ME TOMORROW can recapture the pick of her early-season form back from a break she may ensure that Star People has to settle for the runner-up spot yet again. Muve On looks best of the remainder.

runners.note: Fairly useful form, finishing runner-up on 4 of his last 5 starts. A prominent showing looks assured back in a maiden.
Well held in 2 outings over 6f in the first half of the summer. Has been gelded.
17/2, tenth of 11 in C&D maiden (good to firm) on debut 64 days ago. Has been gelded.
Speedily-bred sort who looks more one for nurseries based on his 2 efforts this month.
Well held both starts and a likely outsider again.
Down the field both starts to date and will need improvement to get heavily involved.

Raced at 5f, showing fair form when runner-up in maiden/novice events in the spring. Has had a break since finishing well held in the Super Sprint at Newbury in July. Leading claims if close to her best on return followi
Well held in a pair of 6f outings in recent months.
Foaled May 7. 12,000 gns Ardad gelding. Half-brother to 9f/1¼m winner Miss Angel and 11f winner Star Brose. Dam winner up to 9f (2-y-o 6.5f winner). The betting should help guide to expectations.
28/1, promise amidst greenness when fifth of 8 in novice at Redcar (5f, good to firm, 28/1) on debut 7 days ago, not knocked about. Should have more to offer.
150/1, last of 9 in C&D novice (good) on debut last Wednesday. Needs to have come on a lot in a short time.

Foaled February 16. 24,000 gns Tasleet filly. Sister to 7f winner Abbey's Dream. Dam, 9.5f winner, sister to smart winner up to 1m Blue Maiden. Muve On looks the stable first string unless the betting suggests otherwise.
25/1, barely modest form when beaten just over 8 lengths into fourth on C&D debut (heavy) 23 days ago.

races.name: City Electrical Factors Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
races.verdict: A case can be made for all 4 but a chance is taken on AMERICAN LAND, who goes back chasing from an exploitable mark on the back of a breathing operation. Lermoos Legend is in fine form so should be bang there again.

runners.note: Opened chase account at Wincanton in November and doubled tally in another small-field affair at Stratford in March. Rare poor effort at latter track 2 months later and off since, leaving Suzy Smith in that time. More li

Notched 2½m handicap chase double last summer. In good form when twice runner-up behind upwardly-mobile winners in May, latterly long way ahead of Lermoos Legend at Worcester and he stayed 23f well when occupying same sp

Won twice around this time last year, including over C&D and also fourth in this race. Left the impression he should have finished closer still when third of 6 in handicap chase at Cartmel in July and pair of runner-up e

Hasn't always looked the most straightforward but has a fine strike rate in handicaps, winning 5 times overall over hurdles. Didn't look happy from a long way out at Newton Abbot in June and off since but he's had a brea

races.name: WTW Willis Towers Watson Handicap
races.verdict: Perhaps this is the day APACHE OUTLAW finally snaps his losing run. Like the selection, Mercurial hasn't tasted success since 2024 but he's recorded 2 good placed efforts in his last 3 starts. Last year's winner Dragon of Malta is once again bidding for successive victories, and a third in this race in 4 years, having scored here on Monday.

runners.note: All 3 outings at Dundalk at the end of 2025, winning on 7f debut in November before showing better form in defeat in December. Tongue tied first time. Off 9 months ahead of turf and handicap debut. Unexposed.
7/4, didn't need to improve to get off the mark at the tenth time of asking in 4-runner novice at Chester (7f, soft) 11 days ago. More on his plate back in a handicap but Colin Keane takes the ride.
Eleven runs since last win in 2025. 20/1, not seen to best effect (not clear run) when bit below form fifth of 10 in handicap at Laytown (7f) 12 days ago. Being eased another 3 lb can only help.

Recorded back-to-back nursery wins over 6f last year. Right back to his best when ½-length second at Fairyhouse (6f, good to soft) in June and given a break since a lesser run at the Curragh at the end of that month.
Plenty of creditable efforts in defeats but latest Cork effort wasn't one of them. On the back of that he has a first-time visor added to his regular tongue tie.

Won on successive days at this meeting last year (including this race) and could be set to repeat the feat having cashed in on a reduced mark here on Monday, albeit he was helped by the rider of the runner-up easing up p
Course winner but rather in and out this season and ran below form when seventh of 12 at Roscommon (7.4f, good to soft) 22 days ago.
Seventeen runs since last win in 2024 but runner-up over 6f here in May and arrives on the back of a good third of 12 at Roscommon (7.4f, good to soft) 22 days ago. Enters calculations.

Came as close to ending his lengthy losing run as he has in a long time when close third in 7f Galway handicap in August. Backed that up with a respectable second of 9 at Chester (7.6f, good to soft) 10 days ago. Conside
Third in a maiden at Galway last autumn and another promising effort there when fourth of 11 on 7f  handicap debut/reappearance 14 days ago. Entitled to come on for that.
Low-mileage 3-y-o who posted her best effort when sixth of 15 in handicap at Limerick (1m, good to soft) in June. Too free back from 12 weeks off at Gowran since and the drop back to 7f may help
Back to his best this season, winning over C&D and at Roscommon. Another good run when third of 18 at Fairyhouse on Monday.
Yet to win but several good efforts this season, including when second at Leopardstown in June and when fifth here on Monday. Has a race in him.

races.name: Jerroms Financial Group Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
races.verdict: TRALEE GIRL made the most of a good opportunity when opening her account over hurdles at Sedgefield last week and could kick on now she's up and running. She can strike while the iron is hot and go in again, probably at the main expense of Sixpack, who can do better on his second go in this sphere.

runners.note: Well beaten in bumpers/2 hurdles. Needs to learn to settle/jump better if he's to have a future in this sphere.
Underwhelming hurdles debut last autumn but much improved on the level for this yard in the meantime, winning 3 handicaps at up to 1¾m. No surprise to see him do better in this sphere now.

Fairly useful 3-time Flat winner at around 1½m for Michael Bell and placed in listed company on first 2 starts over hurdles for this yard. Put aside a couple of disappointing runs when making the most of a good opportuni
Well backed when making her third start in bumpers a winning one at Newton Abbot in July. Might want a stiffer test now hurdling and Flat-oriented yard without a winner in this sphere since 2022/23.
Well held in bumpers. Goes hurdling now and might be one for the longer term.

races.name: Eddie And Violet Smith Conditions Stakes (GBB Race)
races.verdict: JM JUNGLE has run well in a Group 1 in Ireland since his win in the Bullet here last month and is preferred to Jakajaro, who will be a major threat to the selection if near his best but has been below par the last twice.

runners.note: Most likeable type who has enjoyed an excellent season, bagging 4 handicaps during the summer. Another cracking effort when third to Jm Jungle in the Bullet here (heavy) in August. The type to bounce back from a rare bel

Much improved for the switch to front-running tactics this season, winning 5f handicaps at Newmarket and York in the spring. Held his own in Group races on his next 3 outings. His run of good form has come to a halt the

Group 2 winner at Glorious Goodwood last summer and got his head in front in the listed Bullet over C&D (heavy) at the end of August. Creditable 2¾ lengths fifth of 17 to Comanche Brave in Flying Five at the Curragh (5f,

Gained a first success for this yard over 5f at Doncaster in June and has shaped well on a few occasions since. Too keen for his own good in the Portland at Doncaster (5.6f, good) 10 days ago but the return to a bare 5f

Seemed to excel himself in first-time headgear when second in last season's Nunthorpe. Hasn't hit the same heights since, including well beaten in the Bullet here 23 days ago. A bounce back is needed.
Third win of a productive campaign when landing a big-field sprint at Ayr (5f, soft) last Thursday but faces a very stiff task on these terms.
Useful 2-y-o last season, including a win in a 6f French listed race. This is a belated return to action and a watching brief is the percentage call.

races.name: betting.bet New Betting Sites Juvenile Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
races.verdict: OLLIEROB is in good hands and, with the standard set not at all high, he earns the tentative vote to make a successful debut, with the market likely to offer further clues. Rum Diamond can put his experience to use and is feared most.

runners.note: Down the field in varied events on the Flat for James Owen, looking no easy ride (pulls hard). Has joined another quality yard ahead of his hurdling debut but still looks risky.
Mostly disappointing on the Flat and didn't offer much encouragement when a remote third of 8 (Rum Diamond second) on his C&D hurdling debut 25 days ago.
St Mark's Basilica gelding. Half-brother to 6 winners, including fairly useful hurdler Overpriced Mixer. Dam maiden on Flat (stayed 13f). Market should offer some clues.
6,500 gns 3-y-o, Sottsass gelding. Brother to 2-y-o 7f winner Cormoran. Wears a tongue strap and warrants respect on debut for good yard, particularly if the market vibes are strong.
Fair maiden on the Flat (best effort at 12.5f) but it's a little concerning he was sold out of Joseph Patrick O'Brien's yard for only 2,000 gns.

A modest maiden on the Flat for James Owen but showed aptitude for this discipline fitted with a tongue strap on the back of a breathing operation when second of 8 in a C&D juvenile 25 days ago, albeit not always fluent.

races.name: Edmund & Josie Whelan Memorial Listowel Stakes (Listed)
races.verdict: JAGGED EDGE might be able to give the weight away and land a second successive listed win. Meriden is another who has already won at listed level this season and is second choice ahead of Chica Guerrera, who has been performing well enough in handicaps to think she can make an impact at this higher level.

runners.note: Has progressed into a smart performer for current yard, winning listed race at Killarney (1m, good, 7/2) 32 days ago by 1¼ lengths from Carolina Jetstream. Shouldered with a 3 lb penalty for that but it may not stop him.
Not at his best in 2 outings at the start of the summer but enjoyed his finest hour when winning this 12 months ago and no surprise were he to bounce back to form with a bang.
Useful gelding. 22/1, respectable eleventh of 22 in handicap at the Curragh (1¼m, good to soft) 9 days ago, having to pick way through. Yard is no stranger to success in this race.
Fairly useful filly. 22/1, 12¼ lengths ninth of 10 to Moody in listed race at Gowran (1¾m, good to soft) in May. Significantly down in trip on first outing since. Difficult ask.
Useful filly. Latest win handicap at Down Royal in June. Fine second of 18 in handicap (18/1) at Leopardstown (8.3f, good to firm) 10 days ago. Capable of being very competitive in this higher grade.
Useful filly. Encouraging return when fourth of 8 to Beset in listed race at Naas in March but off since a lesser effort at the Curragh in May. Claims on her peak form.
Back-to-back handicap winner on the Flat last autumn but not seen since a fall over hurdles in May. Out of her depth in this company.
Useful winner in France, notably a listed race at Fontainebleau (1¼m, good to soft) last November. This is a slightly belated reappearance but her top new stable is in good form.

Won 9f maiden at the Curragh last summer. Reappeared with a promising second at Fairyhouse in June but not seen again until fourth of 6 at Punchestown (9f, good) last Tuesday. Has a first-time hood added on the back of t

Has improved in leaps and bounds this season, completing a 5-timer in listed race at Killarney in July. Ran as well as could be expected when 5 lengths seventh of 9 to Blue Bolt in recent Matron Stakes at Leopardstown (1

Siyouni filly from an excellent Coolmore family. Made it third time lucky in 18-runner maiden at Navan (1m, good) 17 days ago but  she'll need a chunk of improvement to get heavily involved at listed level.

Won 1m Leopardstown maiden on reappearance in April. Creditable fifth in 10.5f Naas listed race next time and had little chance from her draw in the Sandringham at Royal Ascot in June. Freshened up since. Remains unexpos

races.name: Paul Ferguson's Jumpers To Follow Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
races.verdict: FEVER DREAM tends to go well fresh and is probably still ahead of his mark back after a breathing operation so is chanced to add a second Warwick success to his tally. Ki Woo might be the one for the forecast.

runners.note: Has been on a largely upward curve ever since switched to fences, winning 8-runner handicap chase at Cartmel over this trip in May before a fine second in valuable handicap at Uttoxeter. Returns in easier race, so 3 lb r

Has thrived over fences this summer, scoring 4 times in small-field contests at up to 23f, and would have won again in a match at Perth a fortnight ago but for a late wobble. Can feature if he stays this new trip.

Two hunter chase wins this year and also a creditable sixth in the Aintree Foxhunter in April. Easy to back and not knocked about on first run for 4 months at Worcester recently and may find this sharpening him up furthe

Built on encouraging return effort when winning 3m handicap chase here in March and still looked ahead of his mark upped to marathon trip at Perth the following month (every chance turning in but faded). Has had a breath

races.name: John Allinson 90th Birthday Handicap
races.verdict: BATTENBURG BELLE has thrived in recent weeks, taking her form up a notch on the back of a sharp exit from the stalls when scoring again at Catterick (6f) 2 weeks ago. She looks a big player in her hat-trick bid from a 5 lb higher mark. Black Missile and Under The Radar can give her most to think about.

runners.note: Thirsk maiden winner as a 2-y-o who is holding his form well from steadily easing mark in defeat this year, equipped with cheekpieces when finishing a creditable sixth at Redcar (5f) 7 days ago. This looks a little less

Maiden who was noted doing good late work when sixth in a C&D handicap 2 starts back and went through his race better without seeing his race out when filling same spot at Leicester (5f) 2 weeks ago. Mark has eased a lit

Largely consistent filly who is enjoying a productive campaign, landing back-to-back 6f handicaps at Catterick in recent weeks. Can make her presence felt again following a 5 lb rise back at the minimum trip.

Bounced back to form to win at Pontefract (6f) in July and followed it up with a solid third of 8 in handicap at Chepstow (6f, good to firm) next time. Easy to overlook his latest Carlisle run (eased off having been deni

Narrow winner of a small-field Thirsk nursery (5f) last summer but she struggled in handful of starts thereafter for Karl Burke as a juvenile. New yard has enjoyed success with similar recruits but others make much great

Fared considerably better than previously when a narrow second over C&D in July but hasn't been in anything like the same form in trio of starts since. Has it to prove quickly returned to the minimum trip.

races.name: Setford Handicap Hurdle
races.verdict: Fitted with cheekpieces for the first time over hurdles, STARSHINE LEGEND produced a big career best when successful at Worcester a month ago and with this further increase in trip in his favour, he can go in again. Getaway With You is back on his last winning mark so he's a big threat, with course specialist Motazzen also of interest given his course record.

runners.note: Enthusiastic front runner with 3 wins to his name over fences. Jumping errors started to creep in over the larger obstacles and similar story over hurdles in May/June, for all he ran up to form when placed the last twice

Fairly useful across both codes at his best. Back on the up for current yard when making most of good opportunity at Sedgefield (2½m) before finishing well held in a competitive Punchestown handicap in late-April. Not in

Very much a Fontwell specialist, gaining fourth win here in 5-runner contest over 19f 2 weeks ago. Well positioned how things panned out on that occasion and up 4 lb but he's as effective at this trip and clearly demands

Fair middle-distance winner on the Flat who shaped nicely under a considerate ride when third on hurdles debut at Uttoxeter in June. Failed to build on that next 2 starts but cheekpieces on first time in this code and bi

Better than ever in a first-time visor when winning 11-runner handicap hurdle at Wincanton (2½m, good) in April, racing clear having jumped more fluently than usual. Handicapper took a dim view with a hefty rise and he w

Won back-to-back small-field handicap chase contests in December, latterly at this venue. Some creditable efforts over fences this summer and while he didn't justify strong market support over C&D from his lower hurdles

Ground-versatile sort who won 4 times around 2½m last season. Back in form when beaten 10½ lengths over a trip that perhaps stretched him at Stratford (3¼m) in April and with his return from 5 months off behind him, he s

races.name: MAC Hardware & Farm Supplies Irish EBF Rated Race
races.verdict: ROMANCE had plenty to spare in a nursery last time and might be able to follow up. Banks of The Boyne is exposed but has proved consistent and may provide the chief threat ahead of Aidan O'Brien's Oklahoma.

runners.note: Wootton Bassett colt out of connections' British Champions Fillies & Mares Stakes winner Hydrangea. Promise on first 2 starts but only seventh of 14 in Convivial maiden at the York Ebor meeting (good to soft) 32 days ago

Took another step forward to get off the mark in 10-runner maiden at Galway (7f, good) last month. Backed it up with a good third of 8 in conditions event at Roscommon (7.5f, good, 7/2) 35 days ago. Colin Keane rides.
Fair form. Fifth of 14 in maiden (16/1) at Down Royal (7f, good) 18 days ago, worst of draw. A bit more will be needed to land a first success here.
Winner of maiden at Leopardstown in August. 5/1, creditable third of 6 in nursery at the Curragh (7f, good to soft) since. Should go well again.
Improved effort with a tongue tie added (retained) when winning 10-runner nursery at Down Royal (7f, good, 7/1) 18 days ago, readily. Probably the one to beat if in similar form.
Thrice-raced maiden. 40/1, ran no sort of race last of 12 in maiden at Roscommon (7.5f, good) 35 days ago. Hard to fancy after that.
Close third at Leopardstown (7f, soft) second time up, splitting a now-useful Ballydoyle pair, but hasn't come close to reproducing that since.

races.name: Zulus Gonna Get Ya Mares' Handicap Hurdle
races.verdict: JAMMY JAY is taken to go one better than at Bangor last time and gain a deserved first win over hurdles at the chief expense of Guts And Glory who got off the mark comfortably at Stratford and rates a big threat going into handicaps. Ballylicky Bay appeals as the pick of the rest for minor honours.

runners.note: Runner-up on first 2 starts and advanced her form in first-time tongue tie after 5 months off when readily landing 8-runner novice hurdle at Stratford (19f, good) 4 weeks ago. Has more to offer now going handicapping.

Remains a maiden but hurdling better and running consistently well this season, runner-up for the second time in 4-runner handicap at Bangor (17f, good) 18 days ago. Another bold showing is on the cards off an unchanged
Gained a first win in maiden at Taunton (2m) in April for Tom Lacey but little to enthuse about since, including both starts for new yard. This headstrong sort tries a longer trip now.
Sole hurdles win came for Brian Ellison at Bangor last May. Tongue tied for first time when a solid third of 9 in handicap hurdle at Stratford (2¾m, good to firm) 17 days ago. Not out of things.
Points winner. Maiden under Rules though and cheekpieces fitted for first time when last of 9 in handicap hurdle at Stratford (2¾m, good to firm) 17 days ago. Tongue strap is reached for now.
Successful on sole outing in bumpers and in good form over hurdles this season, second of 11 in handicap at Worcester (2½m, good) in July. Merits consideration after a break.
Runner-up in Irish point. Little to enthuse over in 4 hurdling starts and pulled up on her handicap debut at Bangor (2½m, good) 18 days ago. Cheekpieces go on for first time now.
Modest 11f Flat winner who needed the experience in a pair of hurdle starts last November but unable to advance her form in a trio of handicaps this season.

races.name: Weekend Winners On At The Races Maiden Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
races.verdict: FLIGHT TRACKER is from a smart family and has made a positive start to his career this summer. He can get off the mark. Likely improvers My Boy and Anahona are feared most.

runners.note: Well supported but looked in need of the experience when fifth of 10 in maiden at Kempton (7f) on debut 20 days ago. Likely to improve.
Made appeal on paper but looked in need of the experience when ninth of 11 in maiden at Ascot (7f, good, 12/1) on debut 18 days ago. May need more time.
Promising individual who improved on his encouraging debut effort when second of 8 in novice at Goodwood (1m, soft) 23 days ago. Likely more to come yet.
Foaled May 7. £5,000 yearling, Lope Y Fernandez gelding. Half-brother to 9f winner Kawthar. Dam winner up to 9f (2-y-o 7f winner). Likely a longer-term prospect.
Australia colt who showed plenty of ability when fourth of 8 in maiden at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) on debut last month. Should have learnt plenty from that experience.
Looked very green and finished well held in maiden at Lingfield (7f, AW) on debut 40 days ago. Likely best watched.
Foaled May 1. €68,000 yearling, €45,000 2-y-o, Sioux Nation colt. Half-brother to 3 winners, including French 9.4f winner Classic Sovereign and a winner in Japan. Market check advised on debut.
Foaled April 13. 800,000 gns yearling, Wootton Bassett colt. Half-brother to numerous winners, including top-class winner up to 1½m Ghaiyyath, very smart 1¼m-1½m winner Zhukova. Noteworthy newcomer.
Hinted at ability when fourth of 8 in maiden at Lingfield (1m, AW) on debut 33 days ago. One for longer trips down the line.
Foaled February 7. $300,000 yearling, Upstart colt. Dam, US 1m winner, half-sister to US winner up to 6f (including Grade 3) Lady Scarlet. One to note on debut.
Sent off big odds and ran to just a modest level in maiden at Sandown (7f, soft) on debut 24 days ago. Probably one for handicaps later on.

races.name: Fango Handicap (Div 1)
races.verdict: MISUNDERSTOOD is taken to gain reward for a couple of recent near misses, including over C&D. The hat-trick seeking Supreme Clarets heads the dangers along with Count Palatine and lightly-raced 3-y-o Cotai Eye Joe.

runners.note: Made all at Chester last summer but hasn't really fired in a handful of outings this season, including with a tongue strap added last time.
Produced a career best when scoring at Carlisle (7f, good to soft) last month. Stamina stretched over 8.5f here on heavy since and should find this test more suitable.
His smart 2-y-o form seems a thing of the past but his close seconds over C&D (heavy) and at Thirsk (good to soft) in recent weeks show he's down to a mark he can win from.
Back to form out of the blue to take advantage of a reduced mark at Thirsk (7f, good) in June. Has run creditably in defeat on both outings since and should remain competitive.
C&D winner. Shaped as if still in good form when fourth of 8 in handicap at Chester (7.6f, good to soft, 9/2) 10 days ago. Enters calculations.
Seventeen runs since last win in 2023. 33/1, fared better than of late when fifth of 9 at Thirsk (7f, good to soft) 17 days ago but posed no win threat.
Back to winning ways when making all at Leicester in April and went in again over C&D (good to firm) in May. Off since a disappointing effort back here in June.

Took a step forward when opening his account in 11-runner maiden at Wolverhampton (7f) in April. Better effort in handicaps since when fourth of 13 over 7f at Doncaster (good to firm) in June. Claims if fully primed afte
It took him a while to get off the mark but now on a hat-trick after wins at Ayr (good to firm) and over C&D (heavy) last month. A further 3 lb rise seems unlikely to prevent a bold bid.
Four wins over the extended 1m here but he was second over C&D in June. Another good effort here when third of 10 over 8.5f here (heavy) 24 days ago.

races.name: betting.bet Play Champion Tipster Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
races.verdict: FLASHY BOY would have completed a quick-fire Newton Abbot double last week had he not made a couple of bad mistakes and clearly thriving from his low base, he makes lots of appeal. This represents a drop in class for Yes Day and he's the obvious alternative.

runners.note: Proving more consistent than usual but extended his losing run to 13 all the same when fourth at Worcester a month ago, already held when making a mistake 2 out. Eases in grade here so he really should be a factor.

Quickly resumed winning ways at Market Rasen (3m) in April but that was a decidedly weak affair and he's failed to beat a rival both starts later in the spring. Had a breathing operation ahead of return but assessor look

Completely lost his form after winning over hurdles at Ffos Las in June 2025 but refitting of headgear back over fences helped him stop the slide when runner-up at Newton Abbot in July (3¼m). Was flattered by proximity t

Confirmed the promise of his Stratford run when off the mark under Rules at Newton Abbot in August. Should probably have followed up back there on Friday, held back by a couple of significant errors and he remains one to

races.name: Listowel Arms Hotel Handicap
races.verdict: GLYNDWR had been shaping well until not at his best at Laytown last time and is fancied to bounce back in style off a handy-looking mark wth headgear (both 2025 wins in cheekpieces)  going on for the first time this season. Adrian McGuinness saddles three and his Goal Exceeded could prove the pick in his bid for a third win of 2026. Morehampton and Highbury See See also need factoring in.

runners.note: Winner at the Curragh in March. 66/1, twenty third of 30 in Britannia handicap at Royal Ascot (1m, good to firm) in June. Others look better treated at these weights.
Dual 7f handicap scorer at Naas and Galway later in July. Not in same form at Roscommon and Galways since so bounce back is needed.
Doubled her tally for the season in 12-runner handicap at Roscommon (7.4f, good to soft) 22 days ago by ½ length from Morehampton. Up 3 lb but not taken lightly.

Looked on the up when bagging 9f maiden at the Curragh in April. Off since failing to stay 1¼m when fifth of 6 in conditions event at Naas following month. Returns for his handicap debut (gelded) dropped in trip and rema

Dual 1m Dundalk winner (in cheekpieces) last term. In good form this summer until a below-par sixth of 10 in handicap at Laytown (7f) 12 days ago. Well worth another chance here with headgear fitted for first time this s
Winner of 1m maiden at Dundalk in March and in good nick in handicaps since, third of 5 in handicap at Gowran (9.5f, good to soft) in June. Not ruled out after a break.
On a losing run but back in excellent form of late when placed in handicaps (around 7f) at Gowran and Roscommon. Can go well again.

Resumed winning ways at Dundalk in January but been a mixed bag since, not disgraced with third of 10 in handicap at Laytown (7f) 12 days ago. Tongue strap goes on for first time and cheekpieces are also refitted.
Dual 7f/1m winner last year. Bounced back to form with second of 18 in handicap at Cork (1m, soft) 13 days ago. Goes well on soft ground so must enter calculations.

races.name: Abi And Brad Divorce Handicap Hurdle
races.verdict: LACRIMA wasn't at his best when fourth at Worcester in July but had looked good when an emphatic winner there the time before and is fancied to bounce back in style now freshened up after a break. The handily-weighted Back In The Bay could emerge as the chief threat back hurdling after being pulled up over fences at Bangor.

runners.note: Fairly useful chaser in France. Dominant winner for current yard at Worcester (23f) but a well-held fourth of 5 (evens) in handicap hurdle there (2½m, good to firm) later in July. Freshened up since and well worth anothe

Scored twice at up to 2½m over hurdles last summer. Back to form when second over hurdles at Worcester (23f) in August but pulled up (first-time cheekpieces) back chasing at Bangor (3m, good) 18 days ago. Not without int
C&D winner. Made an encouraging return when fourth at Worcester (23f) in June but has twice failed to build on it at Stratford and Uttoxeter. Blinkers are retried now.
Veteran made a convincing winning return at Cartmel (2¾m) in June. Backed it up with a very good third there but only fifth of 7 returned there last time. Bounce back is needed.
In good nick without winning last season for Emma Lavelle. Returns for new handler after 7 months off and needs to hit the ground running.

races.name: attheraces.com/marketmovers Handicap (Div 1)
races.verdict: LONDONER remains fairly treated and arrives on the back of a good second at Wolverhampton earlier this month. He makes fair appeal. Darn Hot Gallop and Kalokalo can also make their presence felt.

runners.note: Sole success this year came at Lingfield in April but he has largely acquitted himself well in defeat since, latest when second of 12 in handicap at Wolverhampton (1m) 15 days ago. One for the shortlist.

Three-time scorer in 2025 who raised his game further for George Boughey this year, resuming winning ways at Newcastle (1m) in March and back on the up when second at Yarmouth (1m) in June. Proved disappointing on debut

Impressive debut winner at Newbury last October and built on that at the second attempt when winning Doncaster novice on reappearance. Shaped as if amiss in a couple of starts since, however, and has something to prove a

Improved to make a successful reappearance at Yarmouth in April and bettered that form when very good third of 11 at Newbury (1¼m) next time. Nowhere near that form since, though, and no surprise to see blinkers reached

Quite useful form for the Fabre stable in France and may have needed the outing, back from 2 months off, when seventh of 9 on yard/handicap debut at Ripon (1m, soft) 22 days ago. Hood on first time. This run should revea
Won back-to-back races on all-weather in March and April for Martyn Meade but has proved somewhat disappointing on turf since. Bit to prove on first start for new connections here.

Won a pair of all-weather events in November and took a big step forward on handicap debut when scoring at Newmarket on return. Below that level next 3 starts but took a step back in the right direction when fifth in Kem
Made winning start to 2026 over this C&D but not been able to add to that success since, proving disappointing at Chepstow latest. Mark continues to tumble, though.
Registered back-to-back course victories (both 7f) in July but has rather gone backwards since and is tough to recommend at present.

Readily gained a second win of 2026 over C&D in July. Not in quite same form either start since but remains fairly treated if return to this venue sees him back to his best following a gelding operation.
Made a winning start for current yard at this course (7f) in March and added 1m York victory in July. Not really threatened since, however, and others appeal more.

races.name: Fango Handicap (Div 2)
races.verdict: The likeable and consistent TATTIE BOGLE might be able to defy a 4 lb rise for a Brighton success at the start of the month. Glenfinnan's C&D form figures this year are 121 and he's feared most ahead of Folkene and Style of Life.

runners.note: Two C&D wins this year, the latter in August on good ground. Pulled too hard when last of 8 at Ascot since but respected back here.
Back to winning ways at Wetherby (7f) in June and respectable fourths over C&D (good) and at Thirsk (good to soft) on last 2 outings. Likely to be on the premises.

Made all for back-to-back wins at Catterick last autumn. Returned with 2 good placed efforts this spring but hasn't been operating at the same level since, including when only seventh of 8 over C&D latest. Cheekpieces go
C&D winner in June and also second over C&D in July. Back to winning ways at Brighton (7f, good) 3 weeks ago and a 4 lb rise shouldn't prevent another bold bid.
Refused to race at Redcar in July and all but did the same at Newcastle since. One to avoid.

Ground-versatile front runner who recorded back-to-back wins at Chester/Pontefract last summer. Sprung back to life in first-time cheekpieces when length second over 8.5f here (heavy) latest. Player if the headgear works

Left his sole 2-y-o run behind when winning 6-runner novice at Newcastle (6f) in January but has disappointed in a novice and handicap back on turf since. Up in trip after 2 months off and still early days, but arrives w
Course winner. Respectable fourth of 6 in handicap at Newcastle (1¼m) in December (final start for Gemma Tutty). The betting perhaps the best guide to expectations on return for new stable.
Has drawn blank since making a winning start for current yard at Newmarket (7f) last summer but her mark has come down as a result and last week's fourth of 12 at Thirsk (7f, good) was encouraging.

races.name: betting.bet Free Bets Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle
races.verdict: Hard to make a compelling case for any of these but a visor may well sharpen LUCKY IN TAIPAN up and he looks capable of winning a small race for Ben Pauling. Lady Fortune has already tasted success and a short break may well have done her some good, with Winston's Oath a possible improver given the yard he represents.

runners.note: Runner-up in a bumper last summer. Modest form over hurdles, though did run right up to her best when third in maiden company in July. Since left Emma Lavelle.

Narrowly landed a gamble following a breathing operation/break at Market Rasen (2½m) in late-May and resumed winning ways under change of tactics on stable debut at Uttoxeter in July. Race 11 days later may have come too
Well held in bumper and similar story having proved headstrong over hurdles in 2024/25. Raced exclusively on Flat since, finally off the mark at Windsor in June.

Modest middle-distance winner on Flat. Placed twice over hurdles at Newton Abbot this summer before a lesser effort at that venue a month ago. This mark is within range but yard struggling for winners.

Showed a bit on bumper debut but failed to kick on over hurdles for Dylan Cunha. Low-key start to Flat career for James Owen but no surprise if he got it right back over obstacles. Visored first time.
Modest 3-time winner on Flat for Richard Hannon (stays 1½m) but yet to trouble the judge in this sphere and hopes now pinned on breathing operation back from 5 months off.
Remains a maiden but down to a basement level and 2 fourth-place finishes in the spring confirm he's competitive. Has had a breathing operation ahead of return.

Displayed ability in bumpers in 2024. No impact for Max Young last year but did shape fair bit better than on stable debut when third of 9 in handicap hurdle at Worcester (2½m, good) last month. Held back by jumping at B
First sign of ability at Plumpton in May. Back on his correct mark on return and slight step up in trip will suit.
Runner-up in a point but well held all 4 starts under Rules. Handicap debut with cheekpieces on and worth a market check.

races.name: Jet, Peggy & Eamonn O'Carroll Memorial Handicap
races.verdict: An interesting 3-y-o handicap to conclude the card with the vote going to top weight COUNT BEZUKHOV, who has some solid form and there may well be even more to come now that his stamina is drawn out further. Sunrush is unexposed at the trip and can go well again, with Huff'n'puff completing the shortlist.

runners.note: Confirmed debut promise fitted with a tongue tie when winning 1¼m maiden at the Curragh in May, edging ahead late on. That has worked out well and he ran at least as well in defeat under a penalty at Doncaster 7 weeks la

New Bay colt who confirmed promise of 2-y-o debut when winning 1½m maiden at Dundalk in April and showed even better form in defeat on first 2 handicap starts. Failed to make an impact in the Melrose at York last month b

Improved again to win 13-runner maiden at Roscommon in May and ran at least as well in defeat switched to a handicap when fourth of 9 at Down Royal (13f, soft) in June. Off since but has already proven he's capable of go
Took another step forward on his handicap debut when fifth of 9 at Down Royal (13f) in June. Was below form reverting to maiden company at Galway last time, though.

Proved a totally different proposition upped in trip when routing his opposition in a 1¾m handicap at Galway in July. Found life appreciably tougher from a 15 lb higher mark in the Melrose at York subsequently but back d

Australia filly who ran to a similar level as last time when third of 17 in maiden (8/1) at Galway (1½m, soft) 14 days ago, slowly away. Opening mark looks on the stiff side but the combination of first-time cheekpieces
Improved again when opening his account in 18-runner handicap at Navan (1¾m, good, 8/1) 26 days ago, kept up to work. Unexposed at the trip and seems sure to go well again.

Improved further in first-time cheekpieces when off the mark in 16-runner handicap at Limerick (1½m) in June. Could only back up that effort when third of 4 in minor event at Leopardstown but had excuses on his most rece

races.name: attheraces.com/marketmovers Handicap (Div 2)
races.verdict: This can go to HOT AND COLD, who returned to winning ways over C&D earlier this month and hasn't been harshly treated by the handicapper for that victory. Winston's Warrior and Assiri Heights may provide the chief threat.

runners.note: Won 3 times in 2025, with latest victory over 1¼m at Lingfield in December. Yet to really get going this year but is well handicapped again and shaped as if better for the run, back from 4 months off, when eighth at York
Capable of fairly-useful form in Italy for Roberto Biondi but not seen since June and market should prove best guide to claims on UK debut for new yard.
Back on the up when winning 9-runner handicap over C&D (7/4) 19 days ago, keeping on well. 4 lb rise fair and looks sure to go well again.

Posted good second at Kempton on final outing for Hugo Palmer in July and backed that up with creditable fifth at Newcastle (1m) on first run for new yard 3 weeks later. Not in same form back at Kempton latest, though.
Made winning return here (7f) in April and found improvement, back on all-weather surface, when very good second of 13 in handicap at Kempton (7f) 18 days ago, clear of rest. Shortlist material.
Not scored for some time but has been in good form of late, including when creditable second of 11 in handicap over this sort of trip at Beverley 23 days ago. Respected.

Confirmed debut promise when off the mark in smooth fashion in Newmarket novice last summer and ran a cracker under a penalty, back from 14 months off, at same course 5 weeks ago. Failed to make an impact on handicap bow

Off the mark in Leicester maiden on debut this time last year and ran to a similar level in both starts since, including when third of 4 in novice at Leicester (7f, good to firm) on belated return 55 days ago. May have m
Hasn't looked entirely straightforward but did win a pair of 1m handicaps this summer. Finished mid-field at Leicester on Monday and now has his first go on tapeta.

Firmly on the up when doubling his tally at Newbury (1m) in June. Didn't meet expectations over same C&D next time and shaped as if stretched by longer trip when respectable fifth of 13 in handicap at Haydock (1¼m, good
Lightly-raced maiden who built on return effort when second of 11 at Kempton (1m) 13 days ago, closing all way to line. Likely has more to offer now sent handicapping.

races.name: End Of Season Handicap
races.verdict: HORWICH's consistency tempers enthusiasm but he went like the best horse at the weights when splitting Dalamara and Amber Hamur at Musselburgh 2 starts back and with his latest Wolverhampton run easily overlooked, he could well represent a spot of value. The latter rival may emerge as the chief threat, ahead of Bath scorer Buckland Belle. Dalamara also commands respect in an open-looking finale.

runners.note: Quickly resumed her progress when second in a Windsor maiden (5f) in August. Disappointed next time but best not judged harshly on her latest Salisbury fifth having been drawn furthest away from where the main action dev

Free-going sort who did well in the circumstances when third on return/handicap debut at Doncaster (1¼m) in June. However, well beaten both subsequent outings, gelded prior to finishing eighth of 9 at Hamilton (8.3f) 6 w

Much improved following switch to Ed Bethell, landing back-to-back 1m handicaps at Hamilton/Ripon in recent months. Ran another solid race on back of further 5 lb rise when third behind Dalamara at Musselburgh (9f) 4 wee

Went close in 7f Newcastle maiden in March. Overdid the forcing tactics on 1m Haydock handicap debut in May and absent since finishing sixth of 8 at Ayr (7f) the following month (finished lame). Gelded ahead of this and

Inns Of Court filly who showed fair form when landing 8-runner Newcastle (7f) novice in January. Hasn't proved the easiest of conveyances since, though, always behind on back of 5 months off returned to turf at Musselbur

Has won 3 times since switched to turf this year, pulling a little way clear with an in-form rival when landing the odds in 11-runner contest at Bath 20 days ago. All out to hold on then but she commands definite respect

Front runner gained back-to-back wins at Redcar (7f) and Musselburgh (1m) in June. Largely consistent in defeat since and she proved keener than ideal from her wide draw when seventh at Carlisle (7f) 2 weeks ago. Type to

Successful in an all-weather nursery during the winter and proved as good as ever when second at Pontefract (1m) in July. Has largely looked summed up by his mark more recently but may have found 9.5f stretching him at W

Found a bit of progression in first-time cheekpieces when doubling career tally at Musselburgh (9f) in August, (beat Horwich/Amber Hamur) and she ran to a similar level when third under a penalty at Newcastle (1¼m) 3 wee

Free-going sort who boasts a mixed record for this yard but went like the best horse at the weights when second behind Dalamara at Musselburgh (9f) in August. Easy to overlook his latest run (clipped heels and all but ca

Ran his best race when second of 8 to a subsequent winner at Redcar in August but hasn't replicated that in pair of outings this month, only eighth of 10 in a C&D handicap 6 days ago. Others rate more strongly.

races.name: Follow AtTheRaces On X Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
races.verdict: NEWS is bred to be useful and could be up to making a winning debut for her top yard. Ma Blushin Rosie made her effort earlier than ideal at Thirsk last time and is worth another chance to build on her initial promise, while Connie Sachs and Keithaar are other newcomers to keep an eye on in the betting.

runners.note: Foaled April 25. £62,000 yearling, Starspangledbanner filly. Half-sister to 1¼m winner Eagle Emblem. Interesting newcomer.
Has a good pedigree but has offered little in a pair of 7f novices.
Foaled January 27. Cracksman filly. Dam, 2-y-o 1m winner, half-sister to smart winner up to 1m Mother Earth and useful winner up to 1m Ocean Jewel. One to take seriously on debut for top yard.

Too Darn Hot filly shaped encouragingly with fourth of 12 in 6f novice at Redcar on debut but was too free to see things out at Carlisle (6f) since and perhaps isn't ready for this step up in trip just yet.

Foaled April 29. 47,000 gns foal, 30,000 gns yearling, Kameko filly. Half-sister to several winners, including useful German 11f-19f winner Carpathian and 11f winner Yellow Tiger. Top stable 18-66 with its 2-y-o debutant
Dream Ahead filly who showed only greenness when twelfth of 13 in novice at Kempton (7f) on debut 18 days ago. Seemingly needs more time.

Ardad filly who was well backed and showed ability amidst signs of inexperience when third in 7-runner novice at Carlisle (6f) on debut in August. Shaped better than the distance beaten suggests at Thirsk subsequently ha
Holy Roman Emperor who showed only a bit more than on debut when fourth of 5 in novice at Carlisle (7f, good to firm) 42 days ago. Possibly more one for nurseries after this.
Has shown nothing on either of her 2 starts. Cheekpieces now reached for.
Ran best race back up in trip when fifth of 10 in novice at Yarmouth (7f, good) 23 days ago. Has each-way claims, especially if taking another step forward.

races.name: Download The At The Races App Fillies' Handicap
races.verdict: Preference is for INSIDE STORY, who has upped her game of late and didn't get the clearest of runs when second at Wolverhampton last month. Afraj and Merry rate the principal dangers.

runners.note: Opened her account at third time of asking here this time last year and has found improvement this season, finishing runner-up in back-to-back Wolverhampton handicaps (both 7f) in recent months. Likely player.
Won 2 of her 4 starts last year but not seen since disappointing effort at Thirsk 12 months ago. May well need this outing on tapeta debut. Hood on first time/had breathing operation.
Started 2-2 in fillies maidens at Wolverhampton last winter and wasn't far off landing the hat-trick over this C&D. Largely remained in good form since but handicapper may have control for now.
Bagged third victory at Lingfield in 9-runner handicap back in May. 4 lb higher on first start since and will likely need to find improvement to score again.
Raced only on all-weather, winning 7f Kempton maiden last month before close second in handicap over same C&D a week later. May have more to offer yet.
Much improved when narrowly taking 9-runner handicap at Kempton (7f, 11/1) 27 days ago by neck from Merry. Just 2 lb higher here and must be of interest on tapeta debut.

Justified support with a much-improved effort at Goodwood (7f) under this rider in June and followed up with the minimum of fuss at Chester a week later. Finds herself off a career-high mark on first outing since here, h
Progressive filly who won a handicap at Newbury on her return in June and improved on that when good second of 7 at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) last month. Likely to give another good account.
Off the mark when making all in 11-runner novice at this course (6f) in June. However, shaped as if amiss at Carlisle since and has questions to answer now.
Landed a 6f novice at Newbury last summer but has largely disappointed since, coming home last of 11 in 6f handicap at Kempton 17 days ago. Lots to prove in a first-time hood.
C&D winner who did enough to suggest she remains in form when sixth of 13 in minor event at Doncaster (1m, good to firm) 11 days ago. Back down in trip.
Course winner but is in a lull at present, finishing only sixth of 8 in handicap (12/1) at this course (1m) 19 days ago. Has work to do.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Handicap
races.verdict: Not as competitive as the numbers suggest and KOFFEE AND KALE looks to have found a very good opportunity to gain a first win of 2026 on the back of an improved recent Wolverhampton second. The reliable My Mate Mackley is next on the list in his bid for a third victory ahead of in-form duo Long Shot and Deadline.

runners.note: Landed 5f novice here in March for Karl Burke. Best run for current yard when fourth at Lingfield (5f, all-weather) but too free when seventh of 9 in handicap at Wolverhampton (5f) 15 days ago. Hood/tongue strap go on fo
Winless this season but took a step forward in a refitted visor (retained) with second of 9 in handicap at Wolverhampton (5f) 7 days ago. Weighted to go close off the same mark.

Fabled Spirit rates a big threat though on the back of her breakthrough Lingfield success, while both Sir Griflet and Edwardtheninth can play a prominent role too.

Hanney Girl is feared most on the back of her very good Catterick second, while the returning duo of Courageous Sioux and Dance Of Angels both bring potential on their handicap debuts and also need factoring into this open handicap.

races.verdict: GOLDEN KNIGHT didn't enjoy the rub of the green when third at Newbury last time and with this return to a longer trip also a positive he looks the way to go in this competitive handicap. C&D scorer Cliff Danger can also go well on his first run for Tom Ellis, while the returning duo Solarize and Urchin remain with potential and could play a part too.
